title: Chatterbox and Higgs AWS Batch jobs silently produced fake 440Hz stub audio instead of real speech
description:
Confirmed by downloading and analyzing the actual WAV output of two real
production AWS Batch jobs (2aafa279 chatterbox, 218a25e7 higgs, both from
2026-09-16's cost-tracking test pass): both produced an identical fake
440Hz sine tone (exact 5.0s capped duration, smooth periodic waveform,
amplitude range matching 0.2*sin(...)*32767) instead of real synthesized
speech -- while reporting status=done with a real audio_url. Indistinguishable
from success to the job API, the cost tracker, and a console operator.

Root causes (pre-existing, not introduced by this session's work):

1. chatterbox was never installed in the worker image (worker-image/
   Dockerfile only bakes in kokoro+qwen; runner.py's RUNTIME_PACKAGES
   runtime-install dict had no chatterbox entry either), so
   `import chatterbox.tts` always raised ImportError, which
   chatterbox.py's own except-ImportError handler silently converted to
   the stub tone. f5 had the same install gap (would fail loudly instead
   since f5.py has no fallback -- still non-functional, just visibly so).

2. higgs.py caught bare `except Exception` around its entire generation
   attempt -- ANY real failure (CUDA OOM, a model bug, a download
   failure) got silently converted to the same fake tone, not just a
   missing package. fish.py's generate() wrapped both its mlx and torch
   paths the same way.

FIXED in commit de76b16 (2026-09-17): added chatterbox and f5 to
RUNTIME_PACKAGES; narrowed higgs.py and fish.py's except clauses to
ImportError only (matching the principle chatterbox.py's own docstring
already argued for -- a missing optional dependency is a legitimate
reason to stub, a real failure during generation must raise so the job
is correctly marked failed).

Also fixed in the same commit: kokoro.py and f5.py's torch fallback
paths now explicitly resolve cuda/cpu device (previously trusted each
library's own default silently) and log the resolved device, for parity
with higgs/chatterbox/qwen and so a real Batch run's device can be
confirmed from CloudWatch logs.

REMAINING WORK (not done yet -- ran out of session time):
- Rebuild and push the worker image to ECR (auritus-worker repo) for the
  fix to take effect in production -- code changes alone do nothing
  until the image is rebuilt/pushed and a new Batch job pulls it.
- After deploying: trigger fresh chatterbox, higgs, fish, and f5 Batch
  jobs (never-before-seen content hash each, no local worker) and
  download+analyze each resulting WAV to confirm real (non-uniform,
  text-length-proportional) audio instead of the 5.0s stub tone.
- Check CloudWatch logs for the new "[kokoro] resolved device=" /
  "[f5] resolved device=" log lines to confirm cuda, not cpu.
- Partially checked: job 44ae8d61 (kokoro, real production Batch job)
  has duration_seconds=15, actual audio duration 36.9s (a real,
  content-length-proportional duration, NOT the 5.0s stub cap) -- but a
  waveform stdev check on the first 5000 samples came back exactly 0.0
  (all-zero), which could be legitimate leading silence/padding or could
  be a second, different problem -- not yet resolved before running out
  of time. Needs a closer look at samples further into the file before
  concluding kokoro's Batch path is fully healthy.
- The worker-image/README.md claims the container is "Built from NVIDIA
  CUDA runtime... Ubuntu 22.04" but the actual Dockerfile uses plain
  `python:3.11-slim` -- docs vs. reality mismatch, unclear if it's stale
  docs or a real gap in GPU driver/runtime library availability inside
  the container. Worth reconciling.
- Lower priority, separate finding: the CLI's local-worker implementation
  (cli/src/auritus/tts/{higgs,chatterbox,fish}.py, used by
  `auritus worker --once` on a user's own machine) has a related but
  distinct issue -- on non-Apple-Silicon platforms these backends
  unconditionally return stub audio by design (not a bug, an intentional
  degraded mode), but cli/src/auritus/tts/fish.py additionally has the
  same bare `except Exception` swallowing real MLX generation errors on
  Apple Silicon itself (line ~91) -- worth narrowing to ImportError there
  too for consistency, separate from the worker-image fix.
